sentences.text: This armored dinosaur measured about five meters in length and stood two meters tall.
The name references the pelvic armor, which resembles the shape of the extinct mammal glyptodon.
Large, asymmetric shields formed a mosaic pattern over the ilia, with small ossicles filling the gaps.
Fossils were discovered in the Naashoibito member of the Kirtland shale at Barrel Springs Creek in San Juan County, New Mexico.
Gilmore first published the genus in 1919 based only on parts of the armor.
Lehman classified it as a nodosaurid in 1981.
Tracy Ford formally described the species in 2000 in the Bulletin of the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science.
The animal belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
It is classified within the class Ornithischia.
Researchers have placed Glyptodontopelta mimus in the subfamily Stegopeltinae with Stegopelta, though others include it within Shamosaurinae.
This nodosaurid lived in New Mexico between 69 and 66 million years ago.
Its range extended from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
A 2004 review considered the name dubious, but Michael Burns argued in 2008 that its distinctive armor validated the genus.
A debate exists regarding its classification, with Michael Burns rejecting Tracy Ford's placement in Stegopeltinae and assigning it to Nodosauridae instead.
